objective: Restore search-provider job-discovery coverage lost by Phase 14.6's flat consolidation, via adaptive per-source query expansion -- targeting only missing/under-covered configured locations, bounded by a per-source cap and the existing Phase 14.6 global budgets.
modified_files: config/search_planner.json (added max_provider_queries_per_source_per_run=2, coverage_min_unique_jobs=5, coverage_min_locations_covered=3, coverage_min_new_jobs=3, coverage_min_completeness=0.4, all env-overridable)

scripts/daily_search_planner.py (added location-coverage measurement via the existing, unmodified location_taxonomy.py; adaptive round loop in execute_daily_plan(); _job_snapshot() now also captures location+completeness per job)

scripts/test_phase14_6_daily_planner.py (its own _cfg() fixture updated with the new Phase 14.7 config keys, max_provider_queries_per_source_per_run pinned to 1 so its existing, unmodified assertions continue to exercise exactly the Phase 14.6 behavior they were written for)
not_modified: scripts/generate_run_report.py (Phase 14.6's planner_metrics hook reused unchanged, no further edit needed)

phase_14_5_full_matrix.note: 4 locations x 7 boards, one query per (board, location) pair -- the original, most expensive strategy.

phase_14_6_flat_consolidation.note: 1 OR'd-all-locations query per board -- 75% fewer requests than Phase 14.5, but each provider call is capped at ~10 results regardless of how many locations are combined, losing real coverage.

phase_14_7_adaptive_expansion.note: 1 consolidated query per board (7) + targeted follow-up queries only for boards with insufficient coverage (5), stopped by the global per-run budget before reaching 2 of the 7 boards.

query_counts.note: This run's direct-source count (16) is identical to Phase 14.6's -- Section 10 explicitly leaves direct-source planning unchanged. The search-provider side rose from 7 (Phase 14.6) to 12 (Phase 14.7) queries -- still 57% fewer than Phase 14.5's 28 -- while eligible/scored jobs rose from 27 to 33 (+22%).

location_coverage.honest_finding: Only LinkedIn and Wellfound resolved a usable per-job location for any of their jobs at all -- most of the other 5 boards' real hits produced jobs whose location field did not normalize (via the existing, unmodified location_taxonomy.py) into any single configured city, so they correctly show zero covered cities despite finding real jobs (e.g. Instahyre: 24 unique/14 new jobs, but 0 cities resolved). Nothing was invented to fill this gap -- an uncovered/unresolved location is reported honestly, not guessed.

why_wellfound_and_shine_got_only_1_query.reason: The global max_search_provider_queries_per_run budget (12) was reached partway through evaluating boards in round 2 -- LinkedIn, Indeed, Foundit, Instahyre, and Cutshort (evaluated first, in config order) consumed all 5 remaining slots (7 consolidated + 5 adaptive = 12), so Wellfound and Shine were never reached for a round-2 evaluation this run. This is Section 6's 'stop cleanly, never exceed budget' behavior working exactly as specified -- not a bug. Both remain due again on a future run (never permanently suppressed).

provider_requests_saved.note: 12 search-provider requests this run vs. 28 in the original per-location matrix.

cooldown_behavior.self_collision_fix: A genuine edge case was found and fixed during test-writing (not the live run): when a board's round-1 consolidated query returns zero coverage for every configured location, the naive round-2 'missing locations' query is textually IDENTICAL to round 1's own query -- which would otherwise collide with the cooldown record round 1 itself just wrote a moment earlier in the SAME execution, silently blocking the retry. Fixed by tracking every distinct city-combination already attempted this execution, per board, and shrinking the target set by one (lowest-priority) city whenever the naive combination was already tried -- producing a genuinely different, cheaper probe instead of a wasted duplicate. Covered by the new offline test's Scenario D.
cooldown_behavior.verified_offline: Scenario I/J: an identical query within the cooldown window is skipped on a second immediate plan; estimated_provider_calls == 0.

serper_handling.note: Never called this phase -- You.com (priority order first) succeeded on every one of its 12 requests, so the pool never reached Serper. No code change was made to Serper's credentials or implementation.

test_suite.new_test_file: scripts/test_phase14_7_adaptive_expansion.py (18 checks, Sections 13.A-K, fully offline, real-evidence-shaped replay fixtures, never touches production DB or network)

success_target_assessment.reasonable_coverage_across_configured_lo: partial -- 2 of 7 boards (LinkedIn, Wellfound) show at least one resolved city; the other 5 found real jobs but their location text did not resolve to a single configured city via the existing taxonomy, and 2 boards (Wellfound, Shine) were never re-evaluated this run because the run budget was exhausted first
success_target_assessment.no_duplicate_query_requests: yes -- verified via fingerprint history; the one degenerate same-text collision case is handled by the city-set-shrinking fix
success_target_assessment.no_budget_violations: yes -- exactly 12 of 12 allowed search-provider queries used, never exceeded
success_target_assessment.note: No target number was fabricated; every figure above is a real measurement from this run's temp DB and search_provider_usage_store.
